newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower on spec, options selling.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower on spec, options selling.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended lower Monday, pressured by combined speculative and options-related selling, market sources said.

Prices climbed at the outset, with market participants looking for some follow-through buying after Wednesday's firmer finish. But upward momentum never materialized and prices worked lower the rest of the day, traders said.

Most-active January closed 1.75 cents a lb lower, at 95.40, having ranged from 97.90 to 95.10. Second-month March ended down 1.45 cents, to 99.05, while the remaining months settled 0.65 to 1.15 weaker.

On the charts, traders pegged near-term January support at 95.00 cents, followed by 91.75 cents. On the upside, they said January would need to get above 100.58 cents, the 40-day moving average, before a breakout could occur.

But some industry sources said a breach of the 100.00-cent level may prove difficult ahead of January options expiry on Friday. Open interest in the 100.00 puts remained a relatively hefty 4,225 lots, while 105.00 puts had 2,315 lots open interest.

Although the market has been trending lower since early summer, traders said the approaching winter could limit the market's downside. While freezing temperatures are not likely to hit the Florida citrus belt until the end of the month, any sign of cold weather could prompt a round of short-covering, they said.
